consensus_findings.issue: The function apply() sets rec['not_applied'] when the running scorer code or weights do not match the measured values, but still returns the original sa without altering sa['ok']. This allows a run to pass validation (sa['ok'] remains True) even though the calibrated floor was not applied, violating the intended gating logic.
consensus_findings.evidence:
if code != MEASURED_SCORER_SHA or weights != MEASURED_DIGEST:
            rec["not_applied"] = (f"the running scorer is not the measured one (code {str(code)[:12]}, weights "
                                  f"{str(weights)[:12]}; measured {MEASURED_SCORER_SHA[:12]} / {MEASURED_DIGEST[:12]}): "
                                  f"the 3.5 bar alone")
            return sa
consensus_findings.fix:
After setting rec['not_applied'], the function should also set sa['ok'] = False (or otherwise prevent the run from succeeding) before returning. For example:

            if code != MEASURED_SCORER_SHA or weights != MEASURED_DIGEST:
                rec["not_applied"] = (...)
                sa["ok"] = False
                return sa
